title: FSSD: Feature Fusion Single Shot Multibox Detector

problem.summary: SSD's multi-scale feature pyramid makes cross-scale feature fusion awkward, and its shallow-layer features for small objects lack semantic information and context, while the general recognition-versus-localization trade-off of deep ConvNets remains unresolved.
statements: SSD's feature pyramid detection method makes it hard to fuse features from different scales.
Feature maps of small objects from shallow layers lack semantics, causing poor small-object performance.
Fixed receptive field sizes limit detection of very large or very small objects.
Deeper ConvNet features help recognition but harm localization, and vice versa for shallow features.
Layer-by-layer top-down fusion (FPN, DSSD) is inefficient when many layers must be combined.

evidence.quote: However, SSD’s feature pyramid detection method makes it hard to fuse the features from different scales.
But the problem is that the feature of small objects generated by shallow layers lacks enough semantic information which will lead to the poor performance on small object detection.
But the fixed receptive field size is a limitation to detect too large or too small objects.
The main trade-off of object detectors which are based on ConvNets is that the contradiction between object recognition and location.

background.summary: The paper builds on SSD, and compares its fusion design against top-down fusion (FPN, DSSD, SharpMask), multi-layer concatenation (HyperNet, ION) and other SSD variants (RSSD, DSOD), claiming layer-by-layer fusion is inefficient.

relatedWork.relation: base one-stage detector that FSSD enhances
relatedWork.quote: SSD [20] is another efficient one stage object detector.

relatedWork.name: FPN / DSSD / SharpMask
relatedWork.relation: top-down layer-by-layer fusion criticized as inefficient
relatedWork.quote: Top-Down structure like (c) in Fig. 1 is popular recently and has been proved working well in FPN [18], DSSD [7] and SharpMask [24]. But fusing features layer by layer is not efficient enough while there are many layers to be combined together.

relatedWork.name: DSSD
relatedWork.relation: deconvolution-augmented SSD that is accurate but slow
relatedWork.quote: In order to improve the accuracy, DSSD [7] suggests to augment SSD+ResNet-101 with deconvolution layers to introduce additional larges-scale context. However, the speed is slow because of the model complexity.

relatedWork.name: DSOD
relatedWork.relation: trains detectors from scratch with a DenseNet architecture
relatedWork.quote: DSOD [30] investigates how to train a object detector from scratch and designs a DenseNet architecture to improve the parameter efficiency.

relatedWork.name: HyperNet / Parsenet / ION
relatedWork.relation: prior multi-layer feature concatenation before prediction
relatedWork.quote: HyperNet [17], Parsenet [21] and ION [1] concatenate features from multiple layers before predicting the result.

evidence.quote: ConvNets have an excellent ability to extract pyramidal feature hierarchy, which has more semantic information from low to high levels.
This strategy makes SSD lack the capability to capture both the local detailed features and global semantic features.

solution.summary: FSSD adds a lightweight feature fusion module to SSD: features from different layers are transformed to a common size, concatenated, normalized with Batch Normalization, and passed through down-sampling blocks that build a fresh feature pyramid for the multibox heads.
solution.approach: Project selected multi-scale features (conv4_3, fc7, conv7_2) to 256 channels, resize them to 38x38, concatenate and Batch-Normalize them, then apply stride-2 convolutional blocks to generate the new pyramid.
components: 1x1 convolutions reducing source features to 256 channels
bilinear interpolation / max-pooling to a common 38x38 size
down-sampling blocks (3x3 conv with stride 2 plus ReLU) forming the pyramid
VGG16 backbone used as in SSD
SSD multibox prediction heads with NMS

evidence.quote: we propose Feature Fusion SSD(FSSD) by adding a lightweight and efficient feature fusion module to the conventional SSD.
Features from different layers with different scales are projected and concatenated together followed by a Batch Normalization [14] layer to normalize the feature values.

features from different layers with different scales are concatenated together, followed by some down-sampling blocks to generate new feature pyramid, which will be fed to multibox detectors to predict the final detection results.
Our motivation is to fuse the different level features at once with a appropriate way and generate feature pyramid from the fused features.

experiments.summary: Experiments run on PASCAL VOC 2007/2012 and MS COCO with a VGG16 backbone, including an ablation study of fusion layers, fusion operator, normalization and pyramid extractor design on VOC2007, plus speed measurements on a 1080Ti.

evidence.quote: On the Pascal VOC 2007 test, our network can achieve 82.7 mAP (mean average precision) at the speed of 65.8 FPS (frame per second) with the input size 300×300 using a single Nvidia 1080Ti GPU.
FSSD300 can achieve 78.8% mAP, which improves 1.1 points compared with the conventional SSD300.
The results show that concatenation is better than element-wise summation with a large margin of 2.3 points.

limitations.summary: The fusion module costs about 25% extra time over SSD, results on COCO still trail DSOD and DSSD (attributed partly to the VGG16 backbone), and training from scratch is much worse than DSOD.
items: FSSD consumes about 25% extra time relative to SSD because of the added layers.
On COCO, FSSD does not perform as well as DSOD and DSSD.
FSSD512 is slightly lower than DSSD513 in overall accuracy.
Trained from scratch, FSSD300 reaches only 72.7 mAP versus 77.7 for DSOD300.
Fusing conv3_3 brings no accuracy benefit, so the usable fusion range is limited.

evidence.quote: our FSSD consumes about 25% extra time.
Even though our FSSD does not perform as well as DSOD and DSSD
Even though this result is not as good as the DSOD

futureDirections.direction: Combine the fusion module with stronger backbones such as ResNet and DenseNet for better COCO performance.
futureDirections.quote: In the future, it is worth enhancing our FSSD with much stronger backbone networks such as ResNet [12] and DenseNet [13] to get better performance on the MSCOCO dataset

futureDirections.direction: Replace FPN inside Mask R-CNN with the proposed feature fusion module.
futureDirections.quote: replacing the FPN in Mask RCNN [10] with our feature fusion module is also an interesting research field.

deploymentClaims: FSSD300 runs at 65.8 FPS with 300x300 input on a single Nvidia 1080Ti GPU.
FSSD512 runs at 35.7 FPS on a 1080Ti.
Speed comparisons for SSD were re-measured on the same 1080Ti for fairness.
FSSD512 took first place on the VOC2012 leaderboard among one-stage detectors at submission time.

evidence.quote: Our FSSD can run at 65.8 FPS with a 300 × 300 input image on a single 1080Ti GPU.
The FSSD512 takes the first place in VOC2012 leaderboard among all of the one-stage object detectors as of the time of submission.
